title: Isolation of a T-lymphotropic retrovirus from a patient at risk for AIDS (Science, 1983)
summary: In Science of 20 May 1983, Barré-Sinoussi, Chermann, Montagnier and nine co-authors reported isolating a retrovirus distinct from earlier HTLV isolates from a patient with signs that often precede AIDS.
body: Barré-Sinoussi, Chermann, Montagnier and nine co-authors reported in Science on 20 May 1983 (vol. 220, pp. 868-871) the isolation of a retrovirus from a patient with signs that often precede AIDS. Their abstract states that a virus "belonging to the family of recently discovered human T-cell leukemia viruses (HTLV), but clearly distinct from each previous isolate, has been isolated from a Caucasian patient with signs and symptoms that often precede the acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS)". The authors describe a type-C particle budding from the cell membrane, with an internal p25 antigen similar to HTLV p24, transmitted into cord blood lymphocytes; they conclude that such T-lymphotropic retroviruses "may be involved in several pathological syndromes, including AIDS". A separate 1984 Science paper by Gallo and colleagues reported cytopathic isolates designated HTLV-III from 48 subjects.
